examples.en: The teacher taught the students with great dedication.

examples.ko: 모두 열성껏 준비한 덕분에 행사가 잘 끝났어요.
examples.en: Because everyone prepared with such dedication, the event went well.
Thank you so much for helping so wholeheartedly.
Many parents raise their children with great dedication.
We cheered with all our hearts, but sadly lost.

examples.ko: 새로 온 직원이 열성껏 일해서 칭찬을 받았어요.
examples.en: The new employee worked with enthusiasm and got praised.

explain: '열심히'는 어떤 일에든 쓰지만, '열성껏'은 마음과 정성을 다한다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 가르치기, 돕기, 응원하기처럼 남을 위한 일과 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I study Korean hard every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일에든 쓸 수 있는 가장 일반적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most general word, usable with almost any activity.

phrases.en: I prepared the food with care for the guests.
phrases.nuance_ko: '열성껏'처럼 마음을 담는 느낌이지만, 만들기나 준비하기에 더 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 열성껏 it carries heart, but fits making and preparing better.

phrases.en: The neighbors helped with the move wholeheartedly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남을 돕는 일과 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural pairing for helping others.

explain_en: '열심히' fits almost any task, while '열성껏' carries a stronger sense of putting heart and effort into it. It suits things done for others, such as teaching, helping and cheering.

examples.ko: 회사는 올해 안에 새 공장을 완공하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The company decided to complete the new factory within this year.
The contractor finished the building ahead of schedule.

examples.ko: 다리를 완공하는 데 삼 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took three years to complete the bridge.

examples.ko: 건설사는 겨울이 오기 전에 도로를 완공할 거예요.
examples.en: The construction company will finish the road before winter.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 완공한 건물이 상을 받았어요.
examples.en: The building our team completed won an award.

examples.ko: 건물을 빨리 완공하고 싶어도 날씨가 도와주지 않아요.
examples.en: Even if we want to finish the building quickly, the weather won't cooperate.

explain: 완공하다는 짓는 회사나 사람이 주어예요. 건물이 주어이면 '완공되다'를 써요. 공사 뉴스나 안내문에서 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '다 지었어요'라고 말하는 경우가 더 많아요.

phrases.en: The construction company finished building the apartment complex.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '완공하다'보다 '다 짓다'가 더 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk, 다 짓다 is easier than 완공하다.

phrases.en: The company finished the construction on the promised date.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하는 쪽이 주어일 때 자연스럽게 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Natural when the party doing the work is the subject.

phrases.en: The city announced that it had completed the new park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공사 뉴스나 안내에서 자주 나오는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A usage common in construction news and notices.

explain_en: Formal, news-style verb for finishing a building project (새 건물을 완공하다) 완공하다 has the builder (a company or person) as its subject; when the building itself is the subject, use 완공되다. You see it in construction news and notices, while everyday speech more often says 다 지었어요 (we finished building it).

en: to entrust; to leave in another person's hands

examples.en: The chairman left all decisions in the CEO's hands.

examples.ko: 저는 여행 계획을 친구에게 일임하기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to leave the travel plans entirely to my friend.

examples.ko: 이 일은 전문가에게 일임하면 마음이 편해요.
examples.en: If you leave this job to an expert, you can relax.
I'd like you to leave the decision completely to me.
After entrusting something to someone, I try not to interfere.
I'll leave the choice of menu entirely up to you.

explain: '맡기다'보다 딱딱하고, 판단과 결정까지 통째로 맡긴다는 느낌이 강해요. '~에게 ~을 일임하다' 꼴로 쓰고, 일상에서는 '다 맡길게요'라고도 해요. '위임하다'는 권한을 넘기는 쪽에 더 가까워요.

phrases.en: I'll leave all the trip preparations to you.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일임하다'보다 훨씬 부드러운 일상 말이라서 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A much softer everyday word than '일임하다', widely used in conversation.

phrases.en: Please leave this matter entirely to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결정까지 모두 맡겨 달라고 정중하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request to be given full responsibility, including the decisions.

phrases.en: The running of the company was entrusted entirely to him.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일임하다'의 피동 표현이라서, 통째로 맡겨진 일을 주어로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive of '일임하다', used when the thing entrusted is the subject.

explain_en: Hand over everything, full responsibility to one person. It is stiffer than '맡기다' and strongly suggests handing over the judgment and decision completely. It is used as '~에게 ~을 일임하다', and in daily talk people also say '다 맡길게요'. '위임하다' is closer to handing over authority.

t90.ax: I'll leave the choice of menu entirely up to you.

examples.en: I volunteered to give the presentation first.
He took on the hard job of his own accord.
Nobody volunteered to be team leader.
My brother offered to do the dishes, so I just left it to him.

examples.ko: 내가 자청하고 나선 일이니 끝까지 해야죠.
examples.en: I stepped up for this myself, so I have to see it through.

examples.ko: 청소를 자청한 친구 덕분에 빨리 끝났어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the friend who volunteered to clean, it finished quickly.

explain: 남이 시키기 전에 스스로 나서서 맡는다는 점에서 '자원하다'와 비슷해요. 힘들거나 책임이 따르는 일에 특히 잘 어울리고, '발표를 자청하다', '자청해서 하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: He volunteered to take on the cleaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자청해서 + 동사' 형태로 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used in the form '자청해서 + verb'.

phrases.en: I signed up of my own will for the community service.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말인데, 자원하다는 하고 싶어서 신청한다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but 자원하다 feels more like signing up because you want to.

phrases.en: I volunteered for it, so I can't complain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 나서서 맡은 일을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a task one took on of one's own accord.

explain_en: Personally asks for a task, often a hard or thankless one. It is similar to '자원하다' in that you step forward on your own before anyone asks. It suits tasks that are hard or carry responsibility, as in '발표를 자청하다' or '자청해서 하다'.

t90.ax: Nobody volunteered to be team leader.

examples.en: On the weekend I did all the small household chores at once.
There are so many small jobs since this morning that I'm in a whirl.

examples.ko: 잔일은 제가 할 테니 앉아서 쉬세요.
examples.en: I'll do the small jobs, so please sit and rest.

examples.ko: 신입 사원은 잔일도 열심히 해야 해요.
examples.en: New employees have to work hard even on the small jobs.
I'm tired from being bogged down in odd jobs all day.

examples.ko: 큰일 하기 전에 잔일부터 끝내 두세요.
examples.en: Before the big task, finish the small jobs first.

explain: '큰일'의 반대로, 중요하지 않지만 자꾸 생기는 자질구레한 일을 말해요. '허드렛일'과 비슷하게 쓸 수 있고, 집안일이나 회사의 심부름 같은 일에 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I finished all the small chores before leaving work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중요하지 않은 자질구레한 일을 처리한다는 뜻의 기본 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic usage for handling minor, trivial tasks.

phrases.en: I helped with odd jobs at the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잔일'과 비슷하지만 주로 힘들거나 눈에 안 띄는 막일을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 잔일, but mostly refers to menial, unglamorous work.

phrases.en: I was worn down by small chores all day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자잘한 일이 계속 생겨서 힘들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when small tasks keep coming up and wear you out.
phrases.en_equiv: be worn down by small chores

explain_en: As the opposite of '큰일' (a big matter), it means trivial tasks that keep popping up. It can be used much like '허드렛일', and is common for household chores or errand-like work at the office.

en: to reorganize; to reform; to overhaul

examples.ko: 감독이 선수들과 함께 팀을 재정비하고 있어요.
examples.en: The coach is rebuilding the team together with the players.
After exams are over, I rework my study plan.
They decided to refurbish and reorganize the old market.
I took a short break and got myself back in order.

examples.ko: 회사는 조직을 재정비한 뒤에 새 사업을 시작해요.
examples.en: The company restructures its organization and then starts a new business.
The roads are jammed while the road is being redone.

explain: 팀, 조직, 계획, 마음가짐처럼 흐트러진 것을 다시 갖추는 느낌으로 써요. 고장 난 물건을 수리할 때는 그냥 '고치다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I reorganized my mindset during my vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지치거나 흐트러진 마음을 다시 가다듬을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you reset a tired or scattered state of mind.

phrases.en: The team went into reorganization after the season ended.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본격적으로 다시 갖추는 일을 시작한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means starting a full effort to rebuild.

phrases.en: The park was renovated and reorganized.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주어가 장소나 조직일 때 쓰는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A passive form used when the subject is a place or organization.

explain_en: Put things in order again — layout, systems, teams. It gives the feeling of putting something that has gotten loose, such as a team, organization, plan or state of mind, back in shape. For repairing a broken object, people just say '고치다'.

t90.ax: After exams are over, I rework my study plan.

examples.ko: 남편이 다음 달에 부산으로 전근을 가요.
examples.en: My husband is transferring to Busan next month.

examples.ko: 전근 때문에 아이들 학교를 옮겨야 해요.
examples.en: Because of the transfer, we have to move the kids' school.
My colleagues were sad when they heard the news of my transfer.

examples.ko: 지방 전근이 결정돼서 이사 준비를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: My transfer to the provinces was decided, so I'm preparing to move.

examples.ko: 전근은 보통 인사 발표 때 결정돼요.
examples.en: Transfers are usually decided when personnel announcements are made.

examples.ko: 전근 가서 새 동네에 적응하는 중이에요.
examples.en: I transferred and am getting used to a new neighborhood.

explain: 같은 회사나 기관 안에서 다른 지역이나 근무지로 옮기는 일이에요. 회사를 바꾸는 '이직'과 달라요. '전근 가다/전근을 가다'로 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 아버지가 다음 주에 대구로 전근 가세요.
phrases.en: My father is being transferred to Daegu next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 가장 자연스럽게 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural form in speech.

phrases.en: A transfer order suddenly came.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에서 옮기라고 공식적으로 정해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the company officially orders a move.

phrases.en: I applied for a transfer because of my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 옮기고 싶다고 요청할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you request a move yourself.

explain_en: It means moving to a different region or workplace within the same company or organization. It differs from '이직', which means changing employers. It is commonly said as '전근 가다' or '전근을 가다'.

t90.ax: My husband is transferring to Busan next month.

en: to be entirely responsible for; to pay for something alone

examples.en: Mr. Kim is solely in charge of counseling new students.
Our team took sole charge of that work.
It is hard to handle childcare all by yourself.

examples.ko: 병원에는 환자 안내를 전담하는 직원이 있어요.
examples.en: The hospital has staff dedicated to guiding patients.

examples.ko: 그 프로젝트는 우리 부서가 전담할 거예요.
examples.en: Our department will handle that project alone.

examples.ko: 번역을 전담해 줄 사람을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for someone to handle the translation exclusively.

explain: 한 사람이나 한 부서가 어떤 일을 혼자 도맡을 때 써요. '담당하다'는 그 일을 맡는다는 점만 말하고, '전담하다'는 다른 사람은 하지 않고 그 사람만 한다는 느낌이 더해져요. '업무를 전담하다', '전담 부서'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: The company set up a department dedicated to safety.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전담'이 앞에 붙어 한 가지 일만 맡는 부서나 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 전담 in front, it refers to a department or person that handles only one task.

phrases.example: 이 팀이 고객 문의를 전담하고 있어요.
phrases.en: This team is in charge of customer inquiries exclusively.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 그 일만 맡고 있다는 진행형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A progressive form meaning someone keeps handling only that task.

phrases.en: I am in charge of this work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 가깝지만 '전담하다'와 달리 다른 사람도 함께 일할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning, but unlike 전담하다 other people may also work on it.

explain_en: Use it when one person or one department handles a task alone. 담당하다 only says someone is in charge, while 전담하다 adds that nobody else does it. It appears as '업무를 전담하다' and '전담 부서'.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 모든 고객 정보를 전산화했어요.
examples.en: Our company digitized all of its customer information.

examples.ko: 도서관에서 오래된 책 목록을 전산화하고 있어요.
examples.en: The library is digitizing its old book list.

examples.ko: 병원이 진료 기록을 전산화하면 훨씬 편해요.
examples.en: If a hospital digitizes its medical records, it's much more convenient.

examples.ko: 종이 장부를 전산화하려고 새 프로그램을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a new program to digitize the paper ledger.

examples.ko: 시청에서는 민원 서류를 먼저 전산화할 거예요.
examples.en: The city hall will digitize the civil service documents first.
Even small shops need to digitize their inventory.

explain: 종이나 사람 손으로 하던 일을 컴퓨터로 처리하게 바꾼다는 느낌이라 사무·행정 이야기에서 써요. 보통 자료, 기록, 업무 같은 말이 목적어로 오고, '전산화되다'라는 형태도 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: All the documents have been digitized, so it's more convenient now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전산화하다'는 사람이 하는 일이고, '전산화되다'는 그렇게 바뀐 결과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '전산화하다' is what a person does, while '전산화되다' describes the result of the change.

phrases.en: We need to digitize this material quickly too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼭 해야 하는 일을 말할 때 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach it to say something has to be done.

phrases.en: I'm digitizing old documents now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 지금 진행 중일 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This form is used when the work is currently in progress.

explain_en: It means changing work done on paper or by hand into computer processing, so it is used in office and administrative talk. Objects are usually things like data, records or tasks, and the form '전산화되다' (be digitized) also appears often.

examples.en: This year I'll concentrate on studying English.
This company focuses its efforts on developing new products.
I'm putting my main effort into exercise for my health.
Before the exam, I focused on review.
Which field are you focusing on these days?

examples.ko: 한 가지에만 주력하면 다른 일을 놓칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you focus on just one thing, you may miss other things.

explain: '주력하다'는 '~에 주력하다'로 써서 여러 일 중에 가장 큰 힘을 쏟는 곳을 말해요. '집중하다'는 정신을 한곳에 모으는 느낌이고, '주력하다'는 회사, 팀, 계획의 중심 방향을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. '주력 상품', '주력 분야'처럼 명사로도 써요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀은 고객 서비스에 주력하고 있어요.
phrases.en: Our team is focusing on customer service.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 가장 큰 힘을 쏟고 있는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for what you are currently putting the most effort into.

phrases.en: This shop's main product is bread.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게나 회사가 가장 중요하게 파는 물건을 가리키는 명사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase for the product a shop or company mainly sells.

phrases.en: This year I'm putting my effort into exercise.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주력하다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than '주력하다' and more common in daily conversation.

explain_en: Positively putting your main effort into a goal (공부에 주력하다). 주력하다 is used as '~에 주력하다' to name where you pour the most effort among many tasks. 집중하다 is more about gathering your attention on one spot, while 주력하다 fits the main direction of a company, team, or plan. It also works as a noun-modifier in 주력 상품 (flagship product) and 주력 분야 (main field).

t90.ax: Before the exam, I focused on review.

en: to draft for duty; to second; to reassign

examples.ko: 회사에서 직원 세 명을 행사에 차출했어요.
examples.en: The company pulled three employees for the event.

examples.ko: 구단은 선수를 대표팀에 차출하지 않기로 했어요.
examples.en: The club decided not to release the player to the national team.

examples.ko: 급한 일이 생겨서 다른 부서 사람들을 차출해야 해요.
examples.en: Something urgent came up, so we have to pull people from other departments.

examples.ko: 대표팀이 선수들을 차출하면 시즌 경기가 힘들어져요.
examples.en: If the national team calls up the players, the season games get harder.

examples.ko: 시청에서 공무원을 차출해서 행사를 돕게 했어요.
examples.en: City Hall pulled civil servants to help with the event.
The coach said he would pull me for the team.

explain: 'A를 B에 차출하다'처럼 사람을 목적어로 써요. '뽑다'보다 원래 있던 자리에서 빼 와서 쓴다는 느낌이 강하고, 시키는 쪽의 결정이 중심이에요. 스포츠 기사나 회사 이야기에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The company pulled staff from their usual work for the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 필요해서 사람을 원래 자리에서 빼서 쓸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when taking people from their usual posts because the work needs them.

phrases.en: That player was called up to the national team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차출하다의 피동형으로, 불려 가는 사람 입장에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, said from the point of view of the person called up.
phrases.en_equiv: to be called up to the national team

phrases.en: The coach did not call up the injured player.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차출하지 않는다는 결정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state a decision not to call someone up.

explain_en: Take someone from their post for another job, often urgently. It takes a person as the object, as in 'A를 B에 차출하다'. It feels more like pulling someone out of their original place than simply choosing them with '뽑다', and the decision lies with the one giving the order. You can see it in sports articles and workplace talk.

t90.ax: The coach said he would pull me for the team.

examples.ko: 시청은 다음 달에 새 도서관을 착공할 예정이에요.
examples.en: The city hall plans to break ground on a new library next month.

examples.ko: 아파트를 착공하고 나서 이 년 만에 완성했어요.
examples.en: They finished the apartment building two years after starting construction.

examples.ko: 공사를 착공하려면 허가를 먼저 받아야 해요.
examples.en: To begin construction, you must get a permit first.
Residents were glad at the news that construction on the bridge would begin.
The day construction starts was pushed back because of rain.

examples.ko: 지난해에 착공한 지하철 노선이 곧 완성돼요.
examples.en: The subway line begun last year will soon be complete.

explain: 건물, 도로, 다리처럼 큰 공사를 시작할 때만 써요. 반대말은 '준공하다'(공사를 마치다)예요. 집 청소나 작은 수리를 시작할 때는 쓰지 않고 '시작하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The groundbreaking ceremony for the library is tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공사를 시작할 때 하는 행사를 말하는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for the ceremony held when construction begins.

phrases.example: 다음 주에 도로 공사가 착공에 들어가요.
phrases.en: Road construction starts next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본격적으로 공사를 시작한다는 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news for construction getting properly underway.

phrases.en: The bridge whose construction began last year will soon be finished.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 공사를 시작한 건물이나 시설을 앞에서 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a structure whose construction has already begun.

explain_en: It is used only when a big construction project such as a building, road or bridge begins. Its opposite is 준공하다 (to complete construction). For small jobs like cleaning or minor repairs, just say 시작하다.

examples.en: The company embarked on a new business.
Construction is scheduled to start next week.
The police immediately began their investigation.
Once the materials are gathered, we'll get started on the work.

examples.ko: 연구에 착수하기 전에 계획을 세워야 해요.
examples.en: You need to make a plan before starting the research.
Once the team members got to work, the mood improved.

explain: 착수하다는 일이나 공사, 수사처럼 비교적 큰 일을 실제로 시작할 때 써요. '시작하다'보다 격식 있고 '일에 손을 대다'는 느낌이에요. '수사에 착수하다', '공사에 착수하다'처럼 굳은 짝이 많아요.

phrases.example: 다음 달에 새 다리 공사에 착수해요.
phrases.en: Work on the new bridge will begin next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 굳은 짝말로 큰 공사를 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fixed pairing used when starting a big construction project.

phrases.en: The police began investigating the case.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 수사를 공식적으로 시작했다고 알릴 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in the news to announce that an investigation has officially begun.

phrases.en: I start a new job tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이지만 더 쉽고 일상에서 두루 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but easier and used widely in daily life.

explain_en: 착수하다 is used when actually starting a fairly large task, such as a project, construction, or an investigation. It is more formal than '시작하다' and feels like putting your hand to the work. It has set pairs like '수사에 착수하다' and '공사에 착수하다'.

gh: something begins by itself, no doer

p.n: The replacement is the general word, less formal and not specific to tasks.

examples.en: The manager made the new employee attend the meeting.
The school has students attend the event.
Please don't force the child to attend.
The CEO wants to have all the team members attend.
Many companies have employees attend training.
I asked whether we could have guests attend.

explain: '참석하다'는 본인이 가는 것이고, '참석시키다'는 다른 사람을 가게 하는 거예요. 회사와 학교처럼 위에서 정하는 상황에서 쓰고, 친구 사이에서는 잘 안 써요. 가볍게는 '오게 하다', '보내다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: The company makes employees attend training.
phrases.nuance_ko: '참석시키다'와 뜻이 같고 조금 더 풀어서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 참석시키다, said in a more spelled-out way.

phrases.en: I got my friend to come to the party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가벼운 일상 대화에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy phrase used in casual everyday talk.

phrases.en: The company sends employees to training.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어디에 가게 한다는 뜻으로 일상에서 가볍게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light everyday word meaning to send someone somewhere.

explain_en: Causative — have someone be present at a meeting or ceremony. 참석하다 is going yourself, while 참석시키다 is getting someone else to go. It fits company or school settings where someone in charge decides, and rarely appears between friends. Casually, people say 오게 하다 or 보내다.
